questions.problem:
For the transformation $T,$ defined as

$$
T([\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}])⟶[\begin{aligned}uv \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{u}{v})\end{aligned}]
$$

  

compute the value of the Jacobian determinant at the point where $[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
questions.worked_solution:
Given a transformation 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]\to [\begin{aligned}x(u,v) \\ y(u,v)\end{aligned}],
$$

the Jacobian determinant of $T,$ denoted $\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)},$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Here, we have $x=uv$ and $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{u}{v}).$ 

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & =v & \,\frac{∂x}{∂v} & =u \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & =\frac{1}{u} & \,\frac{∂y}{∂v} & =-\frac{1}{v}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the corresponding Jacobian determinant is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}v & u \\ \frac{1}{u} & -\frac{1}{v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =v\cdot (-\frac{1}{v})-u\cdot \frac{1}{u} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, when $[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],$ the value of our Jacobian determinant is

$$
{\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(1,3)}=-2.
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following shows the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $T,$ given by 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+{v}^{2} \\ v-u\end{aligned}],
$$

is (locally) orientation-reversing?
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that a transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing at the points where the Jacobian determinant is negative:

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}<0
$$

We have

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+{v}^{2} \\ v-u\end{aligned}].
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2u & 2v \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2u\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (2v) \\  & =2u+2v.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the required regions, we solve the following inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}2u+2v & <0 \\ 2v & <-2u \\ v & <-u\end{aligned}
$$

 

Notice that the equation 

$$
v=-u
$$

defines a straight line, and the coordinates of, say, $(-1,-1)$ satisfy the inequality. 

Therefore, the region where the transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing must be the following:

questions.problem:
Which of the following shows the region in the $uv$-plane where the transformation $T,$ given by 

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+2v \\ -2u-{v}^{2}\end{aligned}],
$$

is (locally) orientation-reversing?
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that a transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing at the points where the Jacobian determinant is negative:

$$
\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}<0
$$

We have

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}+2v \\ -2u-{v}^{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2u & 2 \\ -2 & -2v\end{aligned}| \\  & =2u\cdot (-2v)-(-2)\cdot 2 \\  & =-4uv+4.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the required regions, we solve the following inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4uv+4 & <0 \\ -4uv & <-4 \\ uv & >1\end{aligned}
$$

 

This gives the solution $v>\frac{1}{u}$ for $u>0$ and $v<\frac{1}{u}$ for $u<0.$

Notice that the equation 

$$
v=\frac{1}{u}
$$

defines a hyperbola, and the coordinates of, say, $(1,2)$ and $(-1,-2)$ satisfy the inequality. 

Therefore, the region where the transformation is (locally) orientation-reversing must be the following:

questions.problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(4,2)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{u}+{v}^{2} \\ uv\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))≈|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\cdot {{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{⏟}}_{\delta A}
$$

 

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}} & 2v \\ v & u\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot u-v\cdot 2v \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{u}-2{v}^{2} \\ {\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(4,2)} & ={\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{u}-2{v}^{2}\,|}_{u=4\,v=2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{4}-2(2)^{2} \\  & =-7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & ≈|-7|\cdot \delta A \\  & =7\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider a small rectangle $Δ$ whose bottom-left corner is located at the point $(3,1)$ with sides parallel to the coordinate axes in the $uv$-plane and whose area is $\delta A.$ Which of the following gives the best approximation for the area of the image of this rectangle under the action of the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}{u}^{3}-v \\ v-u\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the absolute value of the Jacobian determinant gives the local area scale factor of the transformation at that point:

$$
\text{Area}(T(Δ))≈|\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|\cdot {{\text{Area}(Δ)}_{⏟}}_{\delta A}
$$

 

Computing the corresponding Jacobian determinant, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)} & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂u} & \frac{∂x}{∂v} \\ \frac{∂y}{∂u} & \frac{∂y}{∂v}\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3{u}^{2} & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =3{u}^{2}\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & =3{u}^{2}-1 \\ {\frac{∂(x,y)}{∂(u,v)}|}_{(3,1)} & =(3{u}^{2}-1)\,{|}_{u=3\,v=1} \\  & =3(3)^{2}-1 \\  & =26\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(Δ)) & ≈|26|\cdot \delta A \\  & =26\,\delta A.\end{aligned}
$$
